chapters.title: Fellowship in the light and confession of sin

parts.text: The writer declares the Word of life from the testimony of those who heard, saw, and handled what was manifested. Eternal life, which was with the Father, has been revealed. This witness invites the readers into fellowship with the Father and his Son Jesus Christ and is written so their joy may be full.

God is light, with no darkness in him. Claiming fellowship while walking in darkness is false, but walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing through Jesus’ blood. Denying sin deceives oneself and contradicts God. Confessing sins meets his faithfulness and justice in forgiveness and cleansing from unrighteousness.

chapters.title: Obedience, brotherly love, and resistance to deception

parts.text: The readers are urged not to sin, yet are assured of Jesus Christ the righteous as their advocate and the propitiation for the world’s sins. Knowing him is shown by keeping his commandments and walking as he walked. Love for a brother belongs to the light; hatred remains in darkness. Different generations are encouraged in forgiveness, knowledge, and victory, then warned against loving the passing world and its lusts.

Many antichrists already show that it is the last time. Their departure reveals their separation from the faithful, and denial of the Son also denies the Father. The readers should retain what they heard from the beginning, abide in the truth taught by their anointing, and be ready for Christ’s appearing.

chapters.title: God’s children show righteousness and active love

parts.text: The Father’s love makes believers his children. When Christ appears, they will be like him because they will see him as he is; this hope calls for purity. Sin is the transgression of the law, and the sinless Son appeared to take away sins and destroy the devil’s works. The passage contrasts doing righteousness with committing sin and declares that those born of God do not commit sin because his seed remains in them.

Love distinguishes God’s children from hatred like Cain’s. Christ’s laying down his life shows what love means, and those with resources should help needy brethren in deed and truth. Confidence before God is joined to obedience. His command is to believe in his Son and love one another, with the Spirit confirming his abiding presence.

chapters.title: Test the spirits and love one another

parts.text: The readers must test spiritual claims because many false prophets are abroad. Confessing Jesus Christ come in the flesh marks the Spirit of God; denying him reveals the spirit of antichrist already in the world. God’s children overcome because the one in them is greater than the one in the world. Their response to the apostolic testimony distinguishes truth from error.

Love comes from God, who showed his love by sending his Son for their life and sins. Therefore believers must love one another. His Spirit and confession of the Son attest their abiding in him. Perfect love gives confidence in judgment and casts out fear. Claiming love for unseen God while hating a visible brother is false.

chapters.title: Faith, God’s witness, and assurance of eternal life

parts.text: Faith that Jesus is the Christ is joined to new birth, love, and obedience. Those born of God overcome the world through faith in his Son. God bears witness to Jesus through water, blood, and the Spirit. The Father, Word, and Holy Ghost bear record in heaven as one, while the earthly witnesses agree. God’s testimony is that eternal life is in his Son: whoever has the Son has life.

The letter gives believers assurance of eternal life and confidence that God hears requests according to his will. It urges prayer for a brother’s sin not unto death while distinguishing sin unto death. It closes with assurances concerning God’s children and the Son’s revelation, and warns them to keep from idols.
